--- title: "Common errors and how to fix them" subtitle: "Day 1 - Introduction to Data Analysis with R" author: "Selina Baldauf" institute: "Freie Universität Berlin - Theoretical Ecology" date: today date-format: long format: revealjs: footer: "Selina Baldauf // Common errors" highlight-style: breeze mainfont: Cabinet Grotesk slide-number: true show-slide-number: all incremental: true self-contained: true code-line-numbers: false auto-stretch: false scrollable: false fig-align: center theme: slides.scss execute: echo: true warning: false message: false error: true knitr: opts_chunk: collapse: true comment: "#>" from: markdown+emoji --- ## Errors are how you learn When learning a programming language, you will run into errors all the time. That's completely normal and it's how programming works! ![Artwork by [Allison Horst](https://twitter.com/allison_horst)](img/AllisonHorst/debugging.jpg) ## First things first: Set R to English - The R language setting follows your operating system language by default - Errors might not be in English - hard to find help online . . . #### Fix: Change the R language setting to English ```r # For the current session Sys.setLanguage("en") ``` :::{.fragment} :::{.callout-tip} ## Add it to your .Renviron The `.Renviron` file is read automatically every time you start R. Open the file with: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # install the usethis package # install.packages("usethis") # Open the .Renviron file in RStudio usethis::edit_r_environ() ``` ::: and add the line `LANGUAGE=en` to the file. Save it and restart R. ::: ::: # Most common errors for beginners {.inverse} > and how to deal with them ## Console prints `+` R is not running code anymore and the console only prints `+` ![](img/day1/Console_plus.png) . . . #### How to fix it - Go to the console and hit `Escape`. Then you should see the `>` sign instead of `+` again. - Likely you forgot to close a bracket or a quote somewhere. Go to your script and check where this happened (look for  ![](img/day1/red_x.png)  next to line numbers) ## Syntax errors #### Example ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} mean(c(1, 2, 3)na.rm = TRUE) #> Error in parse(text = input): :1:16: unexpected symbol #> 1: mean(c(1, 2, 3)na.rm #> ^ ``` :::
#### How to fix - Look for missing commas, misspelled arguments, unclosed brackets, ... - Read the error message, it often points you to where the problem is - The RStudio syntax checker warns you **before** you run code with syntax errors - Look for  ![](img/day1/red_x.png)  next to line numbers in your script :::{.fragment} ![](img/day1/errors_syntax.png) ::: ## Error: object not found #### Example ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} variable_A #> Error: #> ! object 'variable_A' not found ``` :::
:::{.fragment} #### How to fix - You are trying to access an object that does not exist. Common reasons: - Typo in the variable name (e.g. you created `variableA` but typed `variable_A`) - You forgot to run the line of code that creates the variable - You forgot to put quotes around a string: `print(hello)` looks for a **variable** named `hello`, but you wanted `print("hello")` ::: ## Package problems :::{.columns} :::{.column width="50%"} #### Could not find function ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} read_csv("data/penguins.csv") #> Error in `read_csv()`: #> ! could not find function "read_csv" ``` ::: - You forgot to **load the package**: `library(tidyverse)` - You have a **typo** in the function name (e.g. `lenght()` instead of `length()`) ::: :::{.column width="50%"} :::{.fragment} #### Package not found ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(thispackagedoesntexist) #> Error in `library()`: #> ! there is no package called 'thispackagedoesntexist' ``` ::: ::: - The package is **not installed**: `install.packages("thispackagedoesntexist")` - You have a **typo** in the package name ::: ::: :::{.fragment} Remember for packages: **install once**, but **load every time** you start R ::: ## File not found When reading data, you might see errors like: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} readr::read_csv("data/penguins.csv") #> Error: #> ! 'data/penguins.csv' does not exist in current working directory: #> 'C:/Users/Selina/Documents/Repos/Teaching/intro-r-data-analysis/sessions/slides'. ``` ::: #### How to fix - Check that you are in the **correct RStudio project** (look at the top right corner of RStudio) - Check the **file name**: is it spelled exactly right? - Check the **folder path**: is the file actually in the `data/` folder? :::{.fragment} :::{.callout-tip} ## Build your path with auto-completion When you start typing a path in RStudio, you can use auto-completion to avoid typos. Start with `""` and then hit tab to see suggestions for files and folders in your project. ::: ::: ## Not all red text is an error - **Errors**: something went wrong and your code did not run - **Warnings**: your code still ran, but R tells you something might be wrong (e.g. `NA` values in your data) - Make sure to **read and understand** warnings - Only ignore them if you know that's okay - **Messages**: just information, e.g. when you load the tidyverse ## What to do when you're stuck :::{.nonincremental} - Read the error message - Check your data: use summary() or View() to see if your data looks the way you expect - Read the function help with ?function_name - Restart R and run your script from the top (Session > Restart R in RStudio) - Search online or ask AI :::
Make sure to **save your scripts regularly**. Sometimes R crashes and you have to start a new R session.

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
